assertions.name: alpha5_factorises_exactly_as_budget_times_average
assertions.source: alpha_5(A) = B_6(A) * <c_5>_A holds identically by definition of the weighted average; checked numerically so that the confound claim rests on an identity that was evaluated, not merely asserted.

assertions.name: budget_is_not_constant_across_atoms
assertions.source: B_6 max/min = 222.043131514113737004911776917283943685273383379603469576271 across A = [2, 3, 4] (n = 6, 9, 12). A constant budget would make the raw and self-normalised comparisons equivalent; a varying one means they are different tests. Threshold is a legibility floor, not a physical scale.

description: Bean qou-oots. alpha/alpha_5_jucys_murphy_central.py tests atom-independence of the Jucys-Murphy central scalar c_5 by comparing SUM_{lam |- 3A, ht=6} w_lam c_5(lam) across A = 2,3,4 with w_lam = dim_q^2/[n]_q!. Since n = 3A that is a CROSS-ATOM comparison at three different n, which is the one use AGENTS.md's notation register and qou-oots requirement R2 both exclude for this weight (SUM_lam w_lam(q) is not constant in n; scope-(b), n-independence required). This probe measures the HEIGHT-6 PARTIAL budget B_6(A) = SUM_{ht=6} dim_q^2/[3A]_q! at each A, and verifies the exact decomposition alpha_5(A) = B_6(A) * <c_5>_A. If B_6 varies across A, a spread in alpha_5 cannot distinguish 'c_5 moved' from 'the budget moved'. <c_5>_A is the producer's OWN third route (alpha_5_at_A_partial_normalized), which its docstring already calls 'the structurally derived normaliser'. NOT a claim that the atom-independence conclusion is wrong -- which route it is read off decides that, and the producer reports three.

cross_atom_spreads.note: The budget column is the confound. alpha_5 = B_6 * <c_5>, so any spread in B_6 propagates into the raw comparison whether or not c_5 moved at all. The self-normalised column is the quantity that is invariant under a lambda-independent rescaling of w (qou-oots R2 / ratio_invariant) and is therefore the one a cross-atom test can be read off.

producer_route_invariance.spread_statistic: The producer reports range/median; this probe's own columns report max/min. Different statistics, both quoted under their own names -- neither is a correction of the other.
producer_route_invariance.triage: AFFECTED IN PRINCIPLE, IMMATERIAL IN FACT. The file does use dim_q^2/[n]_q! in a cross-atom (n = 3A) metric, which is the use AGENTS.md's notation register and qou-oots R2 both exclude scope-(b). But its conclusion is a NEGATIVE reached identically by all three of its routes -- including the self-normalised one R2 admits -- so the weight-family choice cannot rescue or overturn it. The Molien ruling does not require a change here.
